chunks: 428 - Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn A'ith, from Abu Khadija who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The Qaim will not come forth until twelve of the Bani Hashim come forth, all of them summoning men to themselves."

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (The Raiser), a title for Imam Mahdi (a.s)
key_terms.بَنِي هَاشِمٍ: Banu Hashim, the clan of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.w.)
key_terms.يَدْعُو إِلَى نَفْسِهِ: Summoning/calling to themselves, claiming authority or imamate

ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve from Banu Hashim that will appear before the Qaim?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights a specific pre-reappearance sign where twelve Hashemite claimants emerge, creating a period of political fragmentation and competing legitimacy. In Shia eschatology, this 'minor occultation' precursor reflects the historical pattern of Hashemite rivalries, serving as a test for the faithful to distinguish the true Qaim from impostors. The narration underscores the importance of recognizing the Imam's unique signs amidst the confusion of multiple self-proclaimed leaders.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 428 - It is narrated from Fadhl bin Shazan from Washa from Ahmad bin Ayez from Abu Khadija  that he said:
Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Qaim will not come forth until twelve of the Bani Hashim come forth before him, all of them summoning men to themselves.”
